_readme: Single source of truth for every robot/field number. PLACEHOLDER values are marked in _placeholders. Edit, save, then press F5 in the sim (or restart) to reload. Units are in the key names.
_placeholders: turret.servo_speed_deg_per_s, levers.speed_deg_per_s (depends on the servos you buy)
levers.front_deploy_sign / back_deploy_sign (flip if a lever swings the wrong way)
drivetrain.loaded_speed_fraction / strafe_efficiency / accel limits (tune against the real robot)
field.* (check the BIOBUZZ field drawings); heights and flower/hive behaviour are guesses
intakes.* and shooter.* (speeds, capacity, how balls are held and released)

field._layout_note: The floor plan comes from data/field_layout.json (BEE simulator, manual TU02). The numbers below are GUESSES for things that file does not give.
field._hive_note: The hive is a seesaw on top of the A-frame (models in cad/field/). The pivot height is the axle holder height measured from the frame CAD. Rule from the team: at hive_tip_pollen pollen in the raised cell it tips, and the pollen inside at that moment count as scored. They then roll out of the lowered cell and the other cell becomes the raised one. Tilt angle and tip time are guesses.
field._april_tag_note: PLACEHOLDER IDs. Each hive has a tag under each cell (audience side and scoring side). Replace with the numbers from the manual.

pollen._note: Size, weight and bounce are read from data/game_elements.json when it exists; these are the fallback values.

intakes._note: One motor per intake + its feeder. Front = side A (plain Intake in the CAD), back = Intake-Mirrored. Both feeders lead into the shared neck under the shooter.

shooter._note: Two motors on one flywheel. A ball waiting at the neck is launched when the gate is open, its intake/feeder motor runs AND the flywheel is spinning.
shooter._gate_note: ASSUMPTION: something holds pollen at the neck until you want to shoot (a gate/stopper servo). Without one, running a feeder with the flywheel spinning fires straight away. Position > 0.5 = open.

robot._size_note: Measured from the CAD by tools/process_cad.mjs (see models/measurements.json). This box is what collides with walls.
robot._start_note: PLACEHOLDER start pose: near the red alliance wall, facing across the field.

drivetrain._inverted_note: PLACEHOLDER. true = positive power on that motor drives its wheel BACKWARDS, because of how the motor is mounted. On most mecanum robots the left side is like this, which is why real code calls setDirection(REVERSE) on the left motors. Used only when Java code drives the robot.

turret._continuous_note: continuous = true: the turret can turn all the way round, with no end stops (needs a continuous or multi-turn servo and a way to keep the wires from winding up). false: limited to servo_range_deg through the gears.

levers._note: Servo position 0 = stowed (upright, as in the CAD), 1 = deployed. Pivots are in the robot frame (+x right, +y up, -z forward, metres), from models/measurements.json.

limelight._note: Limelight 4 on the turret, looking along the shooter. It does not process images: the sim works out which AprilTags are in view from where the robot and turret are. position_m is in the turret's frame (+x = shooting direction, +y up), measured from the CAD. PLACEHOLDERS: mount_pitch_deg (how far the camera is tilted up), the field of view (82 x 56.2 deg is my figure for the Limelight 4), max range and viewing angle, and tag_size_in.
limelight.name: limelight

odometry._note: Two dead-wheel pods read as encoders. Offsets measured from the CAD (models/measurements.json). Wheel size and ticks are PLACEHOLDERS (goBILDA pod: 32 mm, 2000 ticks/rev).

java._note: Running real OpModes. teamcode_dir: folder with your OpMode .java files; empty = the java/teamcode folder of this project. You can point it at your real TeamCode folder. command: how to start Java (a JDK 11 or newer).
